key_insight: Apparent learning by an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration agent largely disappeared after controlling for shared references, with no statistically distinguishable memory or policy benefit.
engineering_relevance: Migration agents need leakage-resistant evaluation and behavioral validation because reference similarity and PostgreSQL acceptance do not establish correctness.
method: Compare no-memory, persistent-memory, and policy-adapted agents against a nearest-target copy baseline.
Audit reference overlap and rerun evaluation with reference-grouped splits.
Test real PL/SQL behavior, human-gated fixes, and retrieval stability as memory grows.
evidence_signal: Across four studies, 72% of initially held-out units shared training references; a grouped rerun found a memory effect of 0.005 [-0.003, 0.017], while 10–22% of PostgreSQL-accepted units in a separate evaluation were behaviorally incorrect.
watch_item: Growing the knowledge base from 12 to 1,200 entries reduced retrieval margin by 54%, raising concerns about stable write-back at scale.
paper_title: Does a Self-Learning Migration Agent Learn? An Audited Evaluation of Evidence-Graded Experience Memory for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
